chapter: Joining Carter and Goodman in New York
title: Meeting William Schuman and teaching jazz piano at Juilliard; Dick Hyman
summary: Wilson accepts Schuman's invitation to teach jazz piano at Juilliard, and he and Hinton praise Dick Hyman for scoring symphonic pieces for them.

story.theme_name: Teaching jazz: schools, students and advice to the young
story.community_name: Becoming a teacher: jazz in schools and conservatories

blocks.x: And the top ballet dancers, Dolan and Markova, of that day -- and the director was a top man, Moss Hart. And the show, called Seven Lively Arts, played at the Ziegfeld Theatre, which Billy Rose owned -- he bought that theatre. And that lasted for quite awhile, and then I met William Shuman during rehearsals there, and we had a lot of serious talks, and he told me, he was gonna be the new President of Juilliard, and would I come up and start a jazz piano course when he became President, and I said I'd be glad to. And I did. And after
the show, I started in about 1945, I guess, and lasted for about 8 years -- and I taught the jazz piano in summer school.
Well, Dick Hyman was one of your students, wasn't he?
Yes, Dick was one of my students.
One of your great students, and he's proud to say, he used to tell everybody that he was one of your students at Juilliard.

Oh yes, Dick has never forgotten that, and he had such a good feel for me, and Dick has returned the favor so many times -- his latest gift to me was some symphonic scores. I can go now and appear with any symphony orchestra, if I get those type of bookings, and Dick has written some scores for me to feature me on the piano with a symphony orchestra, playing standard songs. And he will never take any pay.

He just did the same thing for me. We did a concert with the Baltimore Symphony Orchestra, and I wrote a tune called 'The Judge Meets the Section', the bass section, and Dick scored it for the symphony orchestra, and I played with the bass section, with the symphony orchestra, all of the basses, and he did the exact same thing.
This is just a beautiful thing, seeing this kind of gratitude being returned for your kindness. Teddy, I think we better knock this off for awhile.
